He is considered one of the greatest tight ends of all time.{{cite web |last1=Scott |first1=J.P. |title=25 Greatest Tight Ends in NFL History |url=https://athlonsports.com/nfl/25-greatest-tight-ends-nfl-history |website=Athlon Sports |access-date=August 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809220024/https://athlonsports.com/nfl/25-greatest-tight-ends-nfl-history |archive-date=August 9, 2022 |date=June 21, 2022}}{{cite web |last1=Fragoza |first1=James |title=13 greatest tight ends of all time from Tony Gonzalez to Jackie Smith |url=https://www.profootballnetwork.com/ranking-top-tight-ends-in-nfl-history/ |website=Pro Football Network |access-date=August 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809220404/https://www.profootballnetwork.com/ranking-top-tight-ends-in-nfl-history/ |archive-date=August 9, 2022 |date=October 24, 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Brandt |first1=Gil |title=Gil Brandt's 14 greatest NFL tight ends of all time |url=https://www.nfl.com/photos/gil-brandt-s-14-greatest-nfl-tight-ends-of-all-time-0ap3000000816049 |website=NFL.com |access-date=August 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809220320/https://www.nfl.com/photos/gil-brandt-s-14-greatest-nfl-tight-ends-of-all-time-0ap3000000816049 |archive-date=August 9, 2022}} Sharpe played [[college football]] for the [[Savannah State Tigers football|Savannah State Tigers]] and was selected by the Broncos in the seventh round of the [[1990 NFL draft]]. During his 12 non-consecutive seasons with Denver, he was selected to seven consecutive [[Pro Bowl]]s and four first-team [[All-Pro]]s, and won two consecutive [[Super Bowl]] titles. In between his Broncos tenure, Sharpe was a member of [[Baltimore Ravens]] for two seasons, receiving an eighth Pro Bowl selection and winning a third Super Bowl title. The first NFL tight end to amass over 10,000 receiving yards, Sharpe retired as the NFL leader in tight end [[reception (gridiron football)|receptions]], receiving yards, and receiving [[touchdown]]s. He was inducted to the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2011.{{cite web|url=http://www.profootballhof.com/hof/member.aspx?PlayerId=279|title=Hall of Famers » SHANNON SHARPE|publisher=profootballhof.com|access-date=September 13, 2014}} Following his retirement, Sharpe appeared as an analyst for ''[[The NFL Today]]'' on [[CBS Sports]] and co-hosted ''[[Skip and Shannon: Undisputed]]'' on [[Fox Sports 1]] with [[Skip Bayless]] from 2016 to 2023. In the 2020s, Sharpe also became a prominent figure in the [[sports podcast]] space, hosting ''[[Club Shay Shay]]'' and [[Nightcap (podcast)|''Nightcap'']]. After departing ''Undisputed'' in 2023, Sharpe joined ESPN and was a weekly analyst on ''[[First Take (talk show)|First Take]]'' until 2025.

'''Edward Shane Lechler'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shane Lechler Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LechSh20.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210321111204/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LechSh20.htm |archive-date=March 21, 2021 |access-date=October 3, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|l|ɛ|k|l|ər}}; born August 7, 1976) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who played as a [[Punter (football)|punter]] for 18 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]] and was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the fifth round of the [[2000 NFL draft]]. Lechler also played for the [[Houston Texans]].

Regarded as one of the greatest punters in NFL history,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brandt |first=Gil |author-link=Gil Brandt |date=June 5, 2018 |title=Gil Brandt's greatest NFL punters of all time |url=http://www.nfl.com/photoessays/0ap3000000817839/gil-brandt%27s-greatest-nfl-punters-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190924143006/http://www.nfl.com/photoessays/0ap3000000817839/gil-brandt%27s-greatest-nfl-punters-of-all-time |archive-date=September 24, 2019 |access-date=September 24, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Lechler was named an [[All-Pro]] nine times during his career, and made seven [[Pro Bowl]]s. He led the league in punting average five times and was the NFL's all-time leader in career punting average for nearly two decades.<ref name="punt-average-leaders" /> Lechler was one of two punters named to the [[NFL 100th Anniversary All-Time Team]], along with Hall of Famer [[Ray Guy]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Battista |first=Judy |author-link=Judy Battista |date=December 6, 2019 |title=NFL's All-Time Team: Defensive backs, special teams revealed |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-s-all-time-team-defensive-backs-special-teams-revealed-0ap3000001084661 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220528081423/https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-s-all-time-team-defensive-backs-special-teams-revealed-0ap3000001084661 |archive-date=May 28, 2022 |access-date=October 3, 2022 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Seth Phillip Wand''' (born August 6, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was a starter for the Falcons in [[Super Bowl XXXIII]]. Before playing in the NFL he was an All-American [[college football]] player for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]]. He took his own life in 2009, an outcome that may have been related to [[chronic traumatic encephalopathy]] that resulted from his football career.
